missionObjectives.title: The Hidden Threat in Earth Orbit
missionObjectives.description: Earth's orbit is crowded — with over 100 million pieces of debris traveling at extreme speeds. These fragments, often smaller than a marble, can cause catastrophic damage to active satellites.
missionObjectives.subDescription: While most detection systems only identify debris larger than 3-5cm, TejoOne aims to push this boundary by using a compact, affordable platform. Our mission: to help build a public debris catalog and make orbit cleaner and safer.

association.title: Espaço ao Cubo
association.subtitle: Youth association dedicated to technology development and promoting education in the space sector
association.intro1: We are a passionate group of students united by the dream of reaching space. Our team brings together engineering students from various disciplines, physicists, designers and legal scholars who work collaboratively to develop the first Portuguese CubeSat for space debris detection, designed and built entirely by students.
association.intro2: Beyond the technical challenge, we believe in the power of education and inspiration. We conduct workshops and educational activities from primary to higher education. We also participate in events and lectures, sharing our passion for space with the community, showing that the sky is not the limit.

techValidation.title: Technological Validation
techValidation.description: Validate internally developed (in-house) components and the integration of COTS (Commercial Off-The-Shelf) components into a 1U CubeSat, meeting all design, structural, and operational requirements.

debrisDetection.title: Debris Detection
debrisDetection.description: Prove the feasibility of detecting space debris equal to or greater than 3 cm using a 1U CubeSat and a custom optical 'star tracker' system. Preliminary orbital parameters of the detected debris will be derived and made available on a public website.

research.title: Research
research.description: Study the behavior and validate the integration of COTS components in the space environment, and acquire the essential technical skills for the development of space systems (learn how to build a satellite).

education.title: Education and Open Source
education.description: Train and inspire future generations of space engineers, and create a repository (with reports, studies, and simulations) to continue space education, including the creation of an open source catalogue of detected debris.

subsystems.title: Subsystems
subsystems.subtitle: TejoOne is composed of several subsystems that work together to ensure mission success

obdh.name: OBDH
obdh.details: TejoOne uses a distributed OBDH architecture designed to eliminate single points of failure. The system connects all subsystems via a CSP CAN bus (with I2C redundancy), allowing the ADCS to assume critical functions if the primary On-Board Computer (OBC) fails. It leverages radiation-hardened components and multiple memory types to ensure data integrity in the LEO environment.
obdh.description: On-board computer with a distributed architecture, responsible for data processing and general satellite control.
obdh.specs: Architecture: Distributed (SPoF Elimination), Bus: CAN (Primary), I2C (Secondary), Storage: 1 Gb Flash (Telemetry), MRAM/FRAM (Critical Data)

obsw.name: OBSW
obsw.details: The software stack is built on the FreeRTOS real-time operating system, chosen for its efficiency and modularity. It implements a layered architecture that separates vital from non-vital modules, ensuring the satellite can always boot into a 'Minimal State' for recovery. The software supports remote firmware updates and utilizes the fail-safe Reliance Edge filesystem to prevent data corruption during power cycles.
obsw.description: On-board software based on FreeRTOS that ensures satellite control, state management, and recovery capability.
obsw.specs: Operating System: FreeRTOS, File System: Reliance Edge, Architecture: Layered (Vital/Non-Vital Modules), Functionality: Remote Firmware Updates

comms.name: COMMS (TT&C)
comms.details: TejoOne utilizes a robust half-duplex communication architecture operating in the UHF band. The system integrates a COTS Murgas transceiver with a custom-built (SRAD - Student Researched and Developed) canted turnstile antenna to ensure quasi-omnidirectional coverage. The system is designed for high reliability, employing GFSK modulation and supporting protocols like CSP and AX.25 to manage telemetry downlink and command uplink.
comms.description: Half-duplex radio communication system for data transmission and reception, ensuring high reliability and coverage.
comms.specs: Band: UHF, Frequency: 437 MHz (UHF), Data Rate: 19.20 kbps, Modulation: Gaussian Frequency Shift Keying (GFSK)

eps.name: EPS
eps.details: The EPS is powered by high-efficiency solar panels mounted on four faces of the CubeSat, managed by a SpaceManic AMUN Power Supply Unit (PSU). The system uses Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) to optimize energy harvesting and stores energy in dual Li-Ion cells. It provides regulated 3.3V and 5V lines to all subsystems, with active protection against overcurrent and latch-ups.
eps.description: Power system with solar panels and batteries for satellite power supply, optimized by MPPT and AMUN PSU.
eps.specs: Solar Panels: 4x side panels (2S1P config.), Peak Power: ~2.48 W per panel, Battery: 2x Li-Ion Cells (approx. 24 Wh), Distribution: 6 controllable power lines (3.3V & 5V regulated)

adcs.name: ADCS
adcs.details: The ADCS is responsible for determining and controlling the satellite's attitude in orbit. It uses sensors such as magnetometers, gyroscopes, and accelerometers to measure orientation, and actuators like magnetorquers to adjust the position as needed.
adcs.description: Attitude determination and control system for satellite orientation.
adcs.specs: Sensors: Magnetometers, Gyroscopes, Accelerometer, Actuators: Magnetorquers

payload.name: Payload
payload.details: TejoOne's payload is a modified Star Tracker that functions as a camera for star navigation and debris detection in orbit. With a resolution of 1280 × 980 pixels and a 21º diagonal field of view, it captures high-precision images for on-board processing. The system integrates a baffle entirely designed by Espaço ao Cubo, optimized to reduce unwanted light and improve detection quality, featuring a Sun Exclusion Angle (half angle) of 22.4°.
payload.description: Modified Star Tracker with optimized baffle, capable of combining star navigation with orbital debris detection.
payload.specs: Type: Camera, Resolution: 1280 × 980 pixels, Field of View: 21º Diagonal, Sun Exclusion Angle (half angle): 22.4º

structure.name: Structure
structure.details: The TejoOne structure is a 1U mechanical platform compatible with the CubeSat standard. Manufactured from 6061-T6 aluminum, the structure provides physical support and protection to internal subsystems, ensuring satellite integrity during launch and operation in orbit.
structure.description: 1U mechanical structure compatible with the CubeSat standard.

missionAnalysis.name: Mission Analysis
missionAnalysis.details: The Mission Analysis department was responsible for defining the most suitable orbit for the scientific mission and the competition, and implementing the Initial Orbit Determination and debris size estimation algorithms via photometric analysis, which will serve as the basis for the data processing platform during the operation phase.
missionAnalysis.description: Determination of the satellite's operating orbit and development of algorithms associated with the scientific mission.
missionAnalysis.specs: Orbit: Circular LEO, Altitude: 510-520 km, Inclination: 30-45°, Orbital Lifetime: 4-5 years
